ai.description: This gecko reaches 9 cm. It is pale brown with a dark lateral stripe and a light-tipped tail. Key features include a slender, cylindrical body and terminal toe pads with a distinct distal notch.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus typus* is best distinguished by its unique, undivided distal subdigital lamellae and the presence of a distinct, dark post-ocular stripe.
ai.habitat: *Hemiphyllodactylus typus* inhabits tropical forests and coastal plantations, often found on tree trunks or rock surfaces from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Indo-Pacific slender gecko is primarily nocturnal, foraging for small invertebrates on tree trunks and walls using its specialized, adhesive toe pads to navigate surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemiphyllodactylus typus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs year-round, peaking during the monsoon and post-monsoon seasons.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Hemiphyllodactylus typus* is primarily found in the Western Ghats and Northeast India, ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters elevation.
